title: CWG 2026 Day 2: Jhandu Kumar Wins Bronze as Lawn Bowlers and Swimmers Keep India's Campaign on Track
excerpt: India's para powerlifter claims a gritty bronze in the men's heavyweight final at Glasgow, while lawn bowlers extend their winning streak and Srihari Nataraj advances in the 50m backstroke.
body:
• Jhandu Kumar won bronze in men's heavyweight para powerlifting with a best lift of 190 kg and 130.9 points, adding to India's medal tally at Glasgow.
  • Ashok Kumar Malik narrowly missed the podium in men's lightweight, finishing fourth with 143.8 points behind three lifters separated by fractions.
  • Lawn bowlers Pinki and Rupa Rani Tirkey won 2-0 against South Africa, while Putul Sonowal overcame the Falkland Islands in a tiebreaker to stay unbeaten.
  • Para-swimmers Karthik Budigina and Ali Imam qualified for finals in the men's 100m freestyle, and Srihari Nataraj reached the 50m backstroke semi-final.

Jhandu Kumar's Bronze

The standout moment of Day 2 at the SEC Centre came from Jhandu Kumar, who lifted 190 kg in his second attempt in the men's heavyweight para powerlifting final to secure bronze with 130.9 points. Weighing just 72.4 kg — the lightest in his group — Kumar posted lifts of 181 kg and 190 kg before narrowly missing 196 kg on his third attempt.

Nigeria's Riluwan Idris took gold with 132.8 points, while England's Matthew Harding claimed silver at 131.0. Kumar's bronze was separated from gold by fewer than two points, reflecting the razor-thin margins at the top of the field.

"For a lifter weighing 72.4 kg to compete against athletes nearly double his body weight and still take bronze — that's where the Halliwick points system rewards pound-for-pound strength."

Heartbreak for Ashok Kumar

India's other medal hope in para powerlifting, Ashok Kumar Malik, came agonizingly close to the podium in the men's lightweight category. His 143.8 points placed him fourth, just behind Malaysia's Bonnie Bunyau Gustin, who took bronze with 153.5 points. England's Mark Swan won gold with 153.9 points in the first medal event of the entire 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Elsewhere in para powerlifting, Sudhir Singh finished sixth in the men's heavyweight with 114.1 points after failing on his third attempt at 211 kg. In the women's events, Jaspreet Kaur placed sixth in the lightweight category with 96.4 points, while Kasthuri Rajamani recorded no mark in the women's heavyweight final.

Lawn Bowlers Continue to Dominate

India's lawn bowlers maintained their perfect start to the Games. In women's pairs, the duo of Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki defeated South Africa 2-0, winning the first set 6-4 and the second 7-5 to move to the top of Section B. It was their second consecutive victory after beating Malta in the opening round.

In the men's singles, Putul Sonowal showed composure under pressure, beating Cecil Alexander of the Falkland Islands in a tiebreaker after splitting the first two sets. Sonowal won the opening set 7-5, lost the second 6-8, then prevailed 1-0 in the decider to remain unbeaten at the top of his section.

Swimmers Advance in Glasgow

Srihari Nataraj, India's top male swimmer, qualified for the semi-finals of the men's 50m backstroke. His heat time will need improvement to challenge for a final spot, but advancing through heats on Day 2 keeps his campaign alive.

In para swimming, Ravi Veera Venkata Budigina (Karthik) clocked 57.10 in the 100m freestyle S12 heats to qualify third, then posted 57.57 in the final to finish fourth — close to the podium but just outside medal range. Ali Imam also qualified for the S13 100m freestyle final, finishing seventh with 1:03.73.

Boxing and Gymnastics

Boxer Jadumani Singh entered the ring in the men's 55 kg division, facing Scotland's Aaron Cullen in the Round of 32. In artistic gymnastics, India's men's team of Tapeshwarnath Das, Swathish KP, Tapan Mohanty and Yogeshwar Singh competed in individual qualification alongside the team final.

Day 3 promises more action in the pool and on the mat, with India's weightlifters including Mirabai Chanu set to begin their campaigns. The cycling squad, featuring Ronaldo Singh Laitonjam in the 1000m time trial, also gets under way.
